item.description:
Fixes:
  • A model with no price read $0.00, the same as free usage. A row that shows a token count beside an amount now shows a dash when those tokens could not be priced. That happens when a model is not in the pricing data yet: Claude Opus 5.5 read $0.00 until LiteLLM and OpenRouter listed it on 2026-09-22. The Models tab, the model breakdown, Agents, the Daily and Monthly rows, the usage chart, the heatmap and the usage attribution rows all follow this. In the same places, a positive amount under half a cent now reads <$0.01 instead of $0.00. Totals shown without a token count beside them are unchanged, and they still count unpriced usage as nothing.

Before you update:
  • Repairing an unwritable history file drops a few stored samples, once. A history file the engine could no longer write is now repaired on the first poll rather than refused, and the repair drops the samples that were making it fail validation. Measured on one real store: 39 samples of 5815 in one series, 0.67%. The polls after it needed no repair.
Features:
  • Hovering a row in a window's history shows what its tokens were. Input, output, cache read and cache write, each with its share as a percentage, under a heading naming the window's date and time span. The whole row is the hover target rather than the token count alone, and each model line carries its own breakdown.
Fixes:
  • Pace and history read "unavailable" for every provider, and stayed that way. A write the engine refused wrote nothing and quarantined nothing, so the next poll met the same file and refused it identically. The refusal was permanent rather than transient, and it takes every window in the batch with it: one series stopped the whole lens reporting pace. The write is now repaired inside a bounded allowance instead of refused. The cost was worse than a blank field - while writes were refused the window in progress stopped gaining readings, and a window that ends with no readings near its end was deleted outright, so a refused write destroyed the window it had been unable to extend. This does not close #370: a separate defect still deletes a window whose reset the provider later revises.
  • One provider's unreadable credential erased every other provider's history. A read that fails now costs only its own window. A card whose read failed keeps what it already had, instead of the failure emptying the lens.
  • A few seconds of drift in a provider's reset time split one window into two. The second of the pair read 0% against the full span's tokens. Readings a few seconds apart are grouped as one window again, and the group reports the reset time most of its readings agree on.
  • The quota cards were recomputed from scratch every time the popover opened. The history strip, the heatmap and the equivalences are drawn from the reopen cache, so they are present when the popover appears rather than arriving a moment after it.
  • The daily chart flashed empty for a frame when the popover opened. A series' rows are folded when the view is constructed, not on its first task tick.

Fixes:
  • The Quota lens could report that no history had ever been recorded, about history that was still on disk. Past windows and When the allowance goes fill on launch and could go empty after the app had been running a while. Nothing was lost - relaunching brought the cards back. A refresh that cannot read any history no longer replaces what is already on screen: quota history accumulates, so a refresh returning nothing after those cards have been filled is that pass failing to answer rather than the history ceasing to exist, and the cards now keep what they have. Why those reads come back empty is still under investigation; this does not claim to have fixed that, it stops it from erasing what was already recorded.

Before you update:
  • Tabs for providers you never set up disappear. v1.18.0 began including configured quota sources in the tab bar alongside local usage, which is right for a provider you use and wrong for one you don't. Codex, Claude and Antigravity are built as cards that always exist, so the presence of a card said nothing about whether anything had been set up, and Codex and Antigravity took a tab on every install. A provider with no credential at all now has no tab. One whose credential exists and cannot be read - a permission problem, a corrupt file - keeps its tab and shows what went wrong.
  • Antigravity's two tabs become one. Its IDE and CLI clients draw on one subscription and had a tab each. They now share one, labelled Antigravity, the arrangement Grok Build and Grok Bot already use: the CLI's usage and the IDE's quota card sit under it together. Your own settings survive the merge - a hidden Antigravity CLI tab stays hidden, and its place in your saved tab order becomes the merged tab's.
Fixes:
  • An agy installed after TokenBar started was never found. Antigravity's CLI discovery cached its answer for the life of the process, including the answer that there was nothing to find. Installing agy while TokenBar was running therefore changed nothing until the next launch, and the card went on reporting the error it had been given before. An empty result is now retried on a later refresh.

Thanks: @iF2007

Before you update:
  • Codex turn counts jump from zero to thousands, and the first launch rescans Codex transcripts once. Codex used to announce a human turn one way and around version 0.145 changed to another; TokenBar recognised only the old shape, so the Daily and Monthly cards read 0 turns for Codex on essentially every day. Nothing was recounted: on every day with Codex activity every other figure is byte-identical before and after - tokens, cost, messages, models - and only the turn column moves. Reading turns out of the old cache is not possible, so the Codex parser version moves 5 to 6 and every Codex shard is rebuilt once on first launch. No other client's cache is touched, and the launch after it is normal speed.
Features:
  • The paid OpenCode Go plan now has a quota card. OpenCode stores the Go plan under a separate api key, and TokenBar read only the Copilot quota that lives in the same file. Its rolling, weekly and monthly windows now appear under the existing opencode client rather than as a new tab.
  • Kiro's monthly allowance now appears as a quota card. Kiro was already recognised as a subscription for attribution, but no quota was ever fetched for it, so the plan had no usage bar.
  • Grok Bot's weekly allowance now appears alongside Grok Build's. The two are separate allowances and only Grok Build's was read. Both now appear together under a Grok Build & Bot tab in Overview and Quota, including on machines with no local Grok usage records.
  • Reading that allowance needs your permission once. Grok Bot keeps its login in your Keychain and the weekly limit cannot be read without decrypting it, so the card says what it needs and waits rather than letting macOS ask out of nowhere. Allow proceeds and the system dialog follows a second or two later; Not now leaves the card as a single grey line, with Allow still there whenever you change your mind. If macOS itself refuses or never answers, the card says so and TokenBar stops asking rather than raising the dialog again every cycle - Allow tries once more when you want it to. The login is used for one thing: asking Grok Bot's usage endpoint what your weekly limit is. TokenBar does not store it, does not log it, and sends it nowhere else. Declining affects that card and nothing else, and once macOS holds the grant only macOS can withdraw it. Having Grok Bot signed in already does not change this: the card still asks, and macOS may still want to confirm - this release is the first time TokenBar reads that item, so there is no prior grant to rely on.
  • Window history grows past twelve rows. The card still opens at twelve, and a link under the list adds twelve more per press until every cycle is on screen. Pressing to exhaustion reaches 32, which is where the engine's fold stops.
Fixes:
  • A quota poll could open a browser tab you never asked for. The quota CLI is documented as non-interactive and is not: with an expired token and no DNS it treats the network failure as an authentication failure and starts an interactive sign-in. TokenBar now resolves the endpoint first and gives up without invoking the CLI when that fails.
  • A window-history card said usage was never recorded, about usage sitting in the same scan. Two different statements were collapsed into one flag - the machine recorded nothing, and the machine recorded it and you have not said which subscription it belongs to - so a client you had not classified was reported as having no records at all. The flag is now decided per subscription.
  • One long model name stretched a whole usage card past the edge of the popover. The layout measured every legend item at its ideal width and took the widest row as the card's own width, so a single entry wider than the popover stretched everything around it. Locally-served model names reach that length easily. Items are now measured against the row they sit on, which lets the label's single-line truncation do the job it was already there to do.
  • An OpenCode Go window could be dated to a cycle that had already reset. The clock was read before the request and held across it, so a reset that expired while the request was in flight still compared as being in the future. It is now read after the response arrives.
  • A cancelled quota poller kept running for the rest of its minute. Closing the popover cancels it, but the sleep it was parked in observed only its own timeout, so the task stayed alive for up to a minute after the window it served had gone.

Thanks: @binhonglee, @savourylie

New:
  • Brand logos for the Cline, jcode, MiMo Code, and gjc tabs, instead of a letter badge.
Improved:
  • The client-tab row now scrolls with a plain vertical mouse wheel, so a mouse without a horizontal-scroll wheel can reach every tab.
Fixes:
  • Antigravity CLI now shows the shared Antigravity quota instead of an empty or duplicate limit card.

New:
  • Tracks five more local AI coding tools: Cline, Antigravity CLI, jcode, MiMo Code, and gjc.
Improved:
  • More accurate cost and per-tool attribution across AI token usage.
  • Corrected Codex usage counts for forked and sub-agent sessions.
  • Antigravity CLI usage is now dated per turn, so the live view and daily totals reflect when each turn actually happened.
Fixes:
  • The app no longer crashes if the usage parser hits an unexpected error.
  • More reliable live usage updates, including for the newly added tools.
